bib.title: Confucius Code Agent: Scalable Agent Scaffolding for Real-World Codebases

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Confucius Code Agent: Scalable Agent Scaffolding for Real-World Codebases", Sherman Wong, Zhenting Qi, Zhaodong Wang, Nathan Hu (core, equal) et al., Meta and Harvard. arXiv 2512.10398 v6 (cs.CL), preprint, dated Feb 4 2026 (v6 stamped 3 Feb 2026). No venue.

COVERAGE: All 29 pages, 91,933 chars, read in full, including the appendices. Reference list skimmed. Figures were not rendered. Only the text was extracted.

CORE CLAIM: Scaffolding matters as much as the model. A hierarchical file-based working memory, threshold-triggered LLM compression (the "Architect agent"), and a note-taking agent that writes persistent Markdown notes let a coding agent hold up on long SWE tasks. A meta-agent tunes the tool prompts.

HEADLINE NUMBERS
- SWE-Bench-Pro public split (731 tasks), mean Pass@1 over 3 seeds. Claude 4.5 Sonnet: CCA 52.7, Live-SWE-Agent 45.8, SWE-Agent 43.6. Claude 4.5 Opus: CCA 54.3 vs Anthropic scaffold 52.0 (system-card figure). GPT-5.2: CCA 59.0 vs OpenAI 56.0 (reported figure). Claude 4 Sonnet: CCA 45.5 vs SWE-Agent 42.7 (Table 1, p7).
- SWE-Bench-Verified (500 tasks), Claude 4 Sonnet: CCA 74.6, OpenHands 72.8, SWE-Agent 66.6 (Table 5, p11).

ABLATIONS
- Table 2 (p8): 100-example SWE-Bench-Pro subset, run only on tasks where both variants completed. Claude 4 Sonnet: 42.0 without advanced context management, 48.6 with it. Claude 4.5 Sonnet: 44.0 (no context management, simple tool use), 51.0 (no context management, advanced tools), 51.6 (context management plus advanced tools). So context management adds only +0.6 on 4.5 Sonnet. The tool-use gain (+7.0) is much larger, and the meta-agent learned it.
- Appendix B (p15): 50 long-context instances where summarisation fired at least once. Haiku 3.5 as summariser resolved 22/50. Sonnet 4 resolved 26/50. The orchestrator was Claude 4 Sonnet. Summary quality matters.
- Table 4 (p10), notes across sessions: 151 instances, Claude 4.5 Sonnet, Run 1 versus Run 2 with notes. Turns 64 to 61, tokens 104k to 93k, resolve 53.0 to 54.4.
- Table 3 (p10): resolve rate by number of files edited. 57.8 (1–2 files, n=294), 49.2 (3–4, n=203), 44.1 (5–6, n=86), 52.6 (7–10, n=38), 44.4 (10+, n=18).

QUOTES
- "Without any context control, many trajectories exceed model token limits and fail to complete, hence the restricted subset." (footnote 2, p9)
- "structured context compression not only prevents overflow but also improves reasoning quality by enforcing periodic consolidation of long-horizon plans." (p9)
- "The note-taking layer encourages agents to record not only successful solutions but also compilation errors, runtime exceptions, and unproductive strategies" (hindsight notes, p5)
- "even a weaker model equipped with a strong agent scaffold (Claude 4.5 Sonnet + CCA at 52.7%) can outperform a stronger model (Claude 4.5 Opus + Anthropic's proprietary scaffold at 52.0%)." (p8)

DESIGN DETAILS RELEVANT TO NOTE 06
- Compression: when context nears configurable thresholds, a separate Architect call replaces older turns with a structured summary. The summary holds goals, decisions, errors and open TODOs. A rolling window of recent raw messages is kept (p4–5, Fig 3).
- Externalised state: per-instance memory tree with analysis.md, implementation_summary.md and todo.md (p4–5). The agent writes todo.md during a run (Appendix E trace).
- The Sonnet summary showed "Phase 1 done, Phase 2 mid-way, next is Run function". Haiku's lost the key details (App. B, p15–16).
- Cross-session notes: a note-taking agent runs asynchronously over trajectories. Notes are Markdown with front-matter, a README index, and project/ versus shared/ folders (App. F).
- Context-separation principle (AX versus UX): the agent gets compressed results and humans get full traces (p3–4).

LIMITS
- Compression is only ablated inside the whole CCA system, on a 100-instance subset. Run-to-run noise and confidence intervals are not given. On 4.5 Sonnet the context-management gain is +0.6.
- Survivor bias: the subset only includes tasks where both variants finished.
- Table 4's +1.4 resolve gain (Run 2 against Run 1, n=151) is small and has no variance estimate. The 151 instances were pre-selected as ones where notes could be distilled. The same tasks were rerun, so this is memorisation of the same task, not transfer to new tasks.
- No test of compaction against context reset, no progress-file or session-lifecycle comparison, and no entropy or note-decay analysis. Note staleness, pruning and conflicts are not studied.
- Comparisons against Anthropic's and OpenAI's scaffolds use their reported numbers, not reruns. The authors could not compare against Claude Code on SWE-Bench-Pro. The 8-issue PyTorch-Bench comparison was judged by experts, so it is qualitative.
- The Meta/Harvard authors are the system's builders. Code is at github.com/facebookresearch/cca-swebench.
- Dated: models are Claude 4/4.5 and GPT-5.2.

BUILDS ON
- SWE-Agent (Yang et al., 2024, NeurIPS 37).
- Live-SWE-Agent (Xia et al., 2025).
- OpenHands (Wang et al., 2024).
- Agentless (Xia et al., 2024).
- SWE-Bench (Jimenez et al., 2023).
- SWE-Bench-Pro (Deng et al., 2025).
- Anthropic, "Effective context engineering for ai agents" (2025) and OpenAI's session-memory cookbook (2025), cited for the context-engineering techniques.

FIGURE CANDIDATE: Fig. 3, p4, "Context compression overview. When the context window approaches configurable thresholds, the Architect agent summarizes earlier turns into a structured plan containing goals, decisions, errors, and open TODOs..." It shows compaction before and after.

FIT AND PROBLEMS
- Fit: partial. The paper is on topic for compaction, externalised memory and cross-session notes. The evidence is thin and entangled with other components. It is best cited as a worked system example, with Table 2 and Appendix B as the only compression evidence. Within the folder, the better homes for its other contributions are probably the context-compaction and memory notes (the 02-context-engineering notes 05 and 06) and the tool-design note (03-tool-design), because its largest measured gain comes from tool-use refinement.
- Extraction was clean. No embedded instructions found.
